# Hataori

> Hataori (機織り, "weaving on a loom") is a Rust engine for simple serial, Rayon, MPI, and hybrid MPI + Rayon data-parallel execution. It is inspired by Distributed.jl's dynamically scheduled `pmap` while keeping Rust's scoped execution and MPI's SPMD model: every entry point is a synchronous function call, results always come back in input order, and the first callback error is reported with its input index.

## Conventions you must know before writing code

- **No default features.** Enable exactly the backends you use: `rayon` (rank-local thread pool), `mpi` (link-time rsmpi), or `rsmpi-rt` (MPIABI runtime loading). `mpi` and `rsmpi-rt` expose the same API and are mutually exclusive; enabling both is a compile error.
- **One contract for every model.** Input is a `Vec<T>`, output is a `Vec<U>` in the same order; every call is synchronous; the callback returns `Result<U, E>` with `E: Display`, and the first error is reported with its zero-based index (`MapError::index()`) or, for `pmap`, a `PmapErrorKind` plus a converged error `key()`.
- **Entry point follows the feature set.** `hataori::map` (serial, no bounds beyond `Display`), `hataori::map_in` on a Rayon `Domain` (`rayon`), and `hataori::pmap` (`mpi`/`rsmpi-rt`; hybrid when `rayon` is also enabled).
- **`pmap` is a collective.** Every rank calls it in the same order with the same communicator and `PmapOptions`; only `options.root` supplies `Some(items)` and receives `Some(results)`, every other rank passes `None` and receives `None`. Items and results cross rank boundaries, so `T` and `U` must be serde-serializable.
- **`rayon` changes what `pmap` means.** MPI-only `pmap` requires `LocalMode::Sequential` and rejects `prefetch: true`; with `rayon` enabled `pmap` is the hybrid entry point, rejects `Domain::sequential()`, and needs a pooled `Domain`.
- **`LocalMode` picks in-pool concurrency.** `Sequential` (one callback at a time), `Outer` (callbacks in parallel; evaluate everything, report the lowest failing index), `Inner` (one callback at a time, nested Rayon inside the callback runs in the same pool).
- **P0/P1 limits.** Exactly one execution domain per rank (`DomainId::ZERO`); the batch size is fixed per call; prefetch is opt-in, default off, and bounded to one batch per remote hybrid domain.
- **`rsmpi-rt` needs `MPI_RT_LIB`.** Set it to the absolute path of the MPIwrapper library before launch; there is no link-time MPI dependency in that build.

## Getting started

- [README](https://github.com/shinaoka/hataori-rs/blob/main/README.md): The repository router — features, MPI prerequisites, smoke examples, the docs developer guide, and links to every design document.
- [Documentation home](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/): Execution-model table, the "where to start" workflow map, and a thirty-second serial example.
- [Getting Started](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/getting-started/): Cargo dependency lines per feature set, per-feature prerequisites, choosing an execution model, and running the tutorial code.
- [Parallel Execution Models](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/guides/parallel-models.html): The four models (serial `map`, Rayon `map_in`, MPI `pmap`, hybrid `pmap`), the `LocalMode` semantics, a model-selection table, and the current P0/P1 limits.
- [Choosing Features and Backends](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/guides/features-and-backends.html): Feature matrix, link-time `mpi` versus runtime-loaded `rsmpi-rt`, and the optional `tenferro` feature.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorials index](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/): One Mandelbrot workload rendered by every execution model; each page quotes a runnable example under `examples/` that CI compiles and runs.
- [0. The workload](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/workload.html): The shared `mandelbrot_common.rs` parameters and per-column kernel every tutorial reuses.
- [1. Serial map](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/serial-map.html): `hataori::map` as the semantic baseline: borrowed closures, no `Send`/`'static`/serde requirements.
- [2. Rayon map_in](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/rayon-map-in.html): Building a `Domain`, verifiable CPU placement, and the three `LocalMode`s on one machine.
- [3. MPI pmap](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/mpi-pmap.html): The collective call shape, `PmapOptions`, root-only input/output, and dynamic batch scheduling across ranks.
- [4. MPI placement collectives](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/mpi-placement.html): `broadcast`, `scatter`, and `gather` for owned serde values alongside `pmap`.
- [5. Hybrid MPI + Rayon pmap](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/hybrid-pmap.html): A Rayon pool on every rank, `LocalMode` inside batches, and the opt-in bounded prefetch.
- [6. Runtime-loaded MPI (rsmpi-rt)](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tutorials/rsmpi-rt.html): Tutorials 3–5 without linking MPI: building MPIwrapper, setting `MPI_RT_LIB`, and sharing the runtime with MPI.jl or mpi4py.

## API reference

- [API Reference](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/api/): Landing page for the rustdoc, built with `--features mpi,rayon` so feature-gated items are visible and labelled.
- [`hataori` rustdoc](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/api/hataori/index.html): Function-level documentation for local and facade APIs; the API landing page also links generated runtime rustdoc.

## Design and status

- [P0 design](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design.html): The implemented synchronous core: the execution-lanes local fan-out (`Lanes`, `map_in_lanes`, `pmap_lanes`, `RayonLanes`), scheduler state machine, wire codec, collective preflight, domain admission, and the acceptance contract.
- [P1 bounded prefetch](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/bounded-prefetch.html): The implemented opt-in prefetch of one batch per remote hybrid domain and its invariants.
- [tenferro adapter](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/tenferro-adapter.html): The non-publishable `hataori-tenferro` adapter running one Hataori lane per caller-held tenferro engine (`TenferroLanes`) for `map_in_lanes` and `pmap_lanes`, with cancellation on lane failure and coordinator exit.
- [Distributed runtime architecture](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/distributed-runtime.html): Accepted Phase A-E architecture and current implementation/acceptance boundaries.
- [Object placement and locality-aware task API](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/object-placement-api.html): Implemented fixed placement, colocation, leases, and migration-ready routing contract.
- [Legacy performance runner](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/legacy-performance-runner.html): Immutable P0/P1 baseline runner and frozen measurement boundary.
- [Phase A transport foundation](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/phase-a-transport-foundation.html): Protocol plus memory, TCP, and MPI transport contract.
- [Phase B structured runtime](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/phase-b-runtime.html): Lifecycle, domains, typed actions/futures, scopes, cancellation, and bounded runtime state.
- [Phase C remote objects](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/phase-c-objects.html): Fixed-placement objects, calls, roots, leases, weak handles, and collection.
- [Phase D migration](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/phase-d-migration.html): Explicit freeze/prepare/commit/activate/retire migration.
- [Phase E algorithms](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/design/phase-e-algorithms.html): Bounded batch algorithms, collectives, facades, and the pending performance gate.
- [Implementation readiness](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/implementation-readiness.html): Scope split, resolved review findings, upstream evidence, and the validation matrix behind the P0 core.
- [Review gate log](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/review-log.html): Pre-implementation and per-task review verdicts.
- [Core acceptance ledger](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/core-acceptance-ledger.html): Maps the P0/P1 core acceptance contract to checked evidence and the `scripts/check-core.sh` entry point.
- [Phase A acceptance ledger](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/phase-a-acceptance-ledger.html): Transport-foundation evidence.
- [Phase B acceptance ledger](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/phase-b-acceptance-ledger.html): Structured-runtime evidence.
- [Phase C acceptance ledger](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/phase-c-acceptance-ledger.html): Remote-object evidence.
- [Phase D acceptance ledger](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/phase-d-acceptance-ledger.html): Migration evidence.
- [Phase E acceptance ledger](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/phase-e-acceptance-ledger.html): Algorithm correctness and outstanding performance status.
- [tenferro acceptance ledger](https://shinaoka.github.io/hataori-rs/tenferro-acceptance-ledger.html): Engine lane adapter evidence behind `scripts/check-tenferro.sh`.

## Agent rules

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/shinaoka/hataori-rs/blob/main/AGENTS.md): Which shared tensor4all agent rules to load, the current implementation status, and where durable architecture changes must be recorded.
- [REPOSITORY_RULES.md](https://github.com/shinaoka/hataori-rs/blob/main/REPOSITORY_RULES.md): Hataori-specific durable constraints on layering, transports, protocol boundedness, object identity, and validation.
